marquee: The Last Places for Los Angeles 2028
World's Top Players · One Last Chance

qualify.headline: Where the world comes to qualify
qualify.body: In 2028, squash makes its Olympic debut at the Los Angeles Games. Before it does, the world's top players will come to Washington for one last chance to earn their place. They have been here before: Bellevue hosted the PSA World Tour Finals in 2024, and the Men's World Championship in 2015. Every match matters. Every point could send a player to the Olympics, or send them home.
qualify.imageAlt: American player Olivia Weaver competing against Nele Gilis at the 2023-24 PSA World Tour Finals in Bellevue, Washington

cities.name: Bellevue
cities.tagline: Where the world has played before.
cities.desc: Host of the 2015 Men's World Championship, the first ever on U.S. soil, and the 2024 PSA World Tour Finals.
cities.alt: Downtown Bellevue, Washington skyline across the water

cities.name: Seattle
cities.tagline: Shares the final qualifier with Bellevue.
cities.desc: Bellevue and Seattle share the last qualification event before the Games. Venue to be announced.
cities.alt: Seattle skyline at golden hour with Mount Rainier behind

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.tagline: Where squash makes its Olympic debut.
cities.desc: The Games come to the Comcast Squash Center at Universal Studios, staged on Hollywood's Courthouse Square backlot. The road ends here.
cities.alt: The Universal Studios globe in Los Angeles. Squash will be played at the Comcast Squash Center on the Universal Studios Lot at the 2028 Games.

history.headline: The world has
history.body: Twice. In 2015, YSK Events brought the Men's World Squash Championship to Meydenbauer Center in Bellevue, the first ever on U.S. soil: 100+ professionals, 25+ countries. In June 2024, the PSA World Tour Finals came to Bellevue with the top eight men and women in the world. YSK is a 501(c)(3) founded by the Khan family, holders of seven World No. 1 rankings.
history.alt: The champion lifting the trophy at the 2015 Men's World Squash Championship, the first ever held on U.S. soil

timeline.title: World-champion exhibitions
timeline.desc: Ramy Ashour, Amr Shabana, and Grégory Gaultier headline exhibitions at PRO Club in Bellevue.

timeline.title: Men's World Championship
timeline.desc: YSK makes history: the PSA World Championship comes to the U.S. for the first time. 100+ pros, 25+ countries, record prize money, an all-glass court at Meydenbauer Center.

timeline.title: PMI Bellevue Squash Classic
timeline.desc: A $200K PSA event brings the world tour back to the Eastside.

timeline.title: The Yusuf Khan Invitational era
timeline.desc: Junior championships and the annual invitational honoring the man who brought squash to the Pacific Northwest.

timeline.title: PSA World Tour Finals
timeline.desc: The season-ending finals came to Bellevue. The top eight men and women in the world, including world number one Hania El Hammamy, competed at the Boys and Girls Club at Hidden Valley Fieldhouse.

timeline.title: The Road to LA
timeline.desc: The final Olympic qualification event for squash comes to Washington. Then, Los Angeles.

partner.headline: Be part of squash's
partner.body: Squash has never been an Olympic sport. In June 2028 the last places for Los Angeles are decided in Washington, with the world's top players on the court. Put your brand beside them, or fund the youth programs that run alongside the event through a 501(c)(3) contribution.
